Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

judge noun

in a court of law

also judges, the judge, sit as judge, presiding judge, judge of a contest

classical

Phaedr. 3.13.3: līs ad forum dēducta est, vespā jūdice
Traupman 195, 335: judge

jūdex, jūdicis m./f.

noun, third declension, masculine or feminine

a judge

In a Roman civil case the jūdex was a private citizen appointed to try it; in modern Latin any judge (Traupman 195). To sit as judge is jūs dīcere (Traupman 195, 335). Also anyone who judges, a critic: quālēs sītis jūdicēs! (Phaedr. 5.5.38). For the judge of a game see referee.

Examples

  • apēs in altā fēcerant quercū favōs: hōs fūcī inertēs esse dīcēbant suōs. līs ad forum dēducta est, vespā jūdice.

    Bees had made their honeycombs in a tall oak; lazy drones said the combs were theirs. The dispute went to court, with a wasp as judge.Phaedr. 3.13.1–3

  • grammaticī certant et adhūc sub jūdice līs est

    the scholars disagree, and the case is still before the judgeHor. Ars 78

  • ēn hic dēclārat quālēs sītis jūdicēs!

    Look, this shows what sort of judges you are!Phaedr. 5.5.38

Other words

  • quaesītor, quaesītōris m. — the presiding judge of a criminal court

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 1.29 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 196, 364: presiding judge

    Lewis & Short: an examiner, an inquisitor; especially the praetor who presided in criminal trials.

See also case, law, referee, judge, legal.

SourcesLewis & Short: judex · Lewis & Short: quaesitor
